title: SCORCH (Spatiotemporal Classification of Regional Compound Heatwaves): software and reproducibility workflow

description: SCORCH (Spatiotemporal Classification of Regional Compound Heatwaves) is the software framework used to identify, cluster, and classify regionally extensive compound heatwaves in the Eastern Mediterranean and Middle East from ERA5-derived daily maximum temperature fields (1-degree grid, April-September 1940-2025), for the associated SCORCH manuscript. Upon publication, this record archives the exact GitHub release (https://github.com/fawazbouhamad/SCORCH) used for the associated article, including the installable Python package and command-line interface, builtin end-to-end reconstruction stages verified against the archived processed-data deposit, R scripts for the log-Gaussian Cox process centroid-concentration model (a relative spatial centroid-concentration summary, not a probability, risk, hazard, or susceptibility estimate) and its occurrence-level five-fold validation, exact ERA5 and NOAA GHCN-Daily retrieval specifications, figure and table generation scripts, curated environment locks, tests, the executable fast reconstruction route from the archived processed data, and a documented provider-level ERA5 reconstruction guide (structurally validated; not executed end to end for this release).
